articles.text:
PsiThera Closes $25 Million Financing to Advance Oral Therapeutics in Immunology
By:
PsiThera via
GlobeNewswire
November 10, 2026 at 07:00 AM EST
ⓘ This article is third-party content and does not represent the views of this site. We make no guarantees regarding its accuracy or completeness.
AbbVie Ventures and Lumination Capital joining existing lead investors Samsara BioCapital and Lightstone Ventures
Financing supports TNFα development candidate nomination and initiation of IND-enabling studies, alongside advancement of oral TL1A inhibitors into lead optimization
Proprietary QUAISAR platform, combined with approach to Physical AI, continues to drive rapid design of optimized oral drug candidates
WATERTOWN, Mass., Nov. 10, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- PsiThera, a biotechnology company harnessing biologically relevant protein states and physical artificial intelligence to create oral drugs for immune and inflammatory diseases, today announced the closing of a $25 million financing. New investors AbbVie Ventures and Lumination Capital participated, along with existing lead investors Samsara BioCapital and Lightstone Ventures, and other existing investors. In connection with the financing, Claire Leurent, Ph.D., MBA, Managing Director at AbbVie Ventures, has joined PsiThera’s Board of Directors.
Proceeds from the financing are expected to fund operations, supporting development candidate nomination and the initiation of IND-enabling studies for the company’s lead oral small molecule TNFα inhibitor, as well as advancement of its oral TL1A program into lead optimization.
The company’s proprietary QUAISAR platform combines physics-based molecular simulation, machine learning, and experimental biophysics into a single closed-loop discovery engine to design novel small molecule therapeutics more efficiently. QUAISAR models protein motion to identify and target transient binding pockets that conventional structure-based design cannot see, enabling the design of small molecules for targets that have been difficult to address with oral therapies. Using this platform, PsiThera advanced the company’s lead TNFα program from hit identification to lead optimization in just four months.
“Our goal is to bring the efficacy of leading biologics into novel oral medicines to improve on their therapeutic profiles. This financing accelerates our progress toward that vision as we advance our oral TNFα program toward development candidate nomination and clinical initiation and expand our pipeline of differentiated immunology therapeutics, starting with TL1A,” said Eric D. Shaff, President and Chief Executive Officer of PsiThera. “We are grateful for the continued support of our existing investors and welcome AbbVie Ventures and Lumination Capital.”
Injectable anti-TNFα biologic therapies are approved across a broad range of immune-mediated diseases. However, an oral therapeutic could have broad application, both as monotherapy and as a combination partner, and provide an additional treatment option to the many patients who have not yet started biologic therapy.
PsiThera’s oral TNFα inhibitors are designed to achieve a differentiated profile to improve the therapeutic index relative to injectables or other oral TNFα inhibitors in development, supporting best-in-class potential.

articles.text:
Nanopath Announces $25 Million Series B Financing to Advance Molecular Testing for Women's Health
News provided by
Nanopath
Nov 10, 2026, 09:00 ET
Share this article
Share this article
Financing co-led by Norwest and SV Health Investors' MedTech Convergence Fund will fund launch of Nanopath's FDA 510(k) study for its point-of-care vaginitis test in support of potential expansion of its pipeline into UTIs and STIs, and build-out of its team ahead of proposed commercialization
CAMBRIDGE, Mass. , Nov. 10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Nanopath , a point-of-care diagnostics company enabling laboratory-quality molecular testing in minutes, today announced the close of a $25 million Series B financing round, which includes $2 million in non-dilutive grant financing. The round is co-led by Norwest and SV Health Investors' MedTech Convergence Fund, alongside strategic participation from the Labcorp Venture Fund. New and existing investors also participated, including Elderberry Ventures, GingerBread Capital, and Alumni Ventures.
As part of the financing, Catherine Kiani, J.D., Managing Partner at Elderberry Ventures, and Mindy Nye, Ph.D., Vice President, Labcorp Diagnostics, have joined the Nanopath Board as Observers.
"Nanopath is developing truly transformative technology with the potential to reshape the molecular diagnostics industry and dramatically improve patient outcomes," said Jeff Crowe, Senior Managing Partner at Norwest. "We are beyond excited to continue supporting the company at this key inflection point."
Nanopath has developed the first clinical diagnostics platform built on plasmonic biosensing. The company's proprietary optical biosensing technology is designed to enable molecular detection without nucleic acid amplification, a step required by PCR-based tests. "We've spent years developing and pressure-testing a fundamentally new approach to molecular diagnostics for patients who have been overlooked for far too long," said Alison Burklund, Ph.D., Co-Founder & Co-CEO of Nanopath. "This funding brings us closer to the next and most important step – translating that innovation into meaningful clinical impact."
The funding will support key milestones toward the potential commercial launch of Nanopath's 15-minute point-of-care vaginitis assay, including manufacturing scale-up and initiation of Nanopath's Food and Drug Administration 510(k) clinical study. Nanopath will also use the funding to expand its team across clinical and commercial functions as it prepares for launch. "We're incredibly proud of the extraordinary team we've built at Nanopath and our shared commitment to transforming women's healthcare," said Amogha Tadimety, Ph.D., Co-Founder & Co-CEO of Nanopath. "We're grateful for the confidence of our investors and excited to build on this momentum as we enter our next phase of growth."
By delivering accurate results during a single visit, Nanopath aims to establish a new standard of care for women's health and expand access to high-quality diagnostics for women across the United States. Over time, the platform is expected to expand to other clinical indications, improving healthcare by making sophisticated diagnostics more accessible at the point of care.
The vaginitis test is currently under development and has not been cleared or approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Commercial availability is subject to successful completion of development activities and applicable regulatory review.

SPARETECH aims to cut manufacturers' spare parts inventory by 60% within three years with AI that ensures parts are available when they are needed
MUNICH , Nov. 10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- SPARETECH, a provider of enterprise AI for spare parts management, today announced it has raised $20 million in Series B funding to help manufacturers cut their spare parts inventory without risking downtime. Blume Equity and Insight Partners co-led the round, with participation from Headline.
Geographic expansion and growth trajectory
Continue Reading
SPARETECH Founders | Dr. Lukas Biedermann & Martin Weber
SPARETECH has established itself in the United States and grown its revenue fivefold since the start of 2024. Over the same period, the company grew its spare parts catalog to more than 40 million verified parts and expanded its network to 15,000 manufacturer and supplier partners. The global rollout of Nestlé, a SPARETECH customer, put 320 plants across 70 countries live in less than a year, further affirming SPARETECH's global enterprise capabilities and speed.
"Every customer we work with wants the same thing: the production line running with less inventory on the shelf. That is the problem we are going to solve with Maintenance teams, and our goal is to cut spare parts inventory by 60% in the next three years, while securing the same uptime."
Martin Weber, CEO and Co-Founder, SPARETECH
Why spare parts stay on the shelf
Spare parts management has long been one of manufacturing's most persistent inefficiencies. A single stockout can halt production and idle an entire line, making plants default to holding extensive spare parts inventories as a safeguard. The result is a substantial amount of capital sitting on the shelf. SPARETECH's 2026 benchmark report puts the average value of spare parts inventory at $169 million per company.
Source: Unlocking cost savings in spare parts management: The 2026 benchmark report on MRO spend, productivity, and working capital , SPARETECH, 2026.
From visibility to availability
Since its founding, SPARETECH has helped customers gain visibility into the parts they hold and standardize their spare parts data, which is the foundation of effective spare parts management. Meaningfully reducing inventory levels, however, requires more than good data. It requires physical action.
SPARETECH is moving the market beyond insights and recommendations toward measurable outcomes: lower inventory with the same uptime. To reach the 60% goal, every maintenance professional needs confidence that the right part will be available when needed, even if it sits on another company's shelf. SPARETECH's AI will secure that availability.
"Every part sitting idle is cash that could be working somewhere else. We are building AI that makes sure the right part is available when a plant needs it and put those idle parts back into circulation, so the money tied up on the shelf can go back to growing the business."
Dr. Lukas Biedermann, COO and Co-Founder, SPARETECH

Primordial Labs: $18 Million Series A Funding To Expand AI-Powered Military Command And Control Platform
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 9:59 AM
Primordial Labs: $18 Million Series A Funding To Expand AI-Powered Military Command And Control Platform
Primordial Labs, a defense technology company developing natural-language command and control software for military systems, has raised $18 million in Series A funding to expand deployment of its Anura platform. The investment will support the company’s engineering and product development operations while accelerating adoption across military vehicles, aircraft, and uncrewed systems. The financing was led by Ballistic Ventures, with participation from existing investors Squadra Ventures and Lockheed Martin Ventures.
Founded in 2021 and headquartered in New Haven, Connecticut, Primordial Labs develops technology that allows military personnel to interact with complex equipment using natural-language instructions.
Its Anura platform functions as a software layer between human operators and the systems they control.
Modern military platforms often incorporate multiple sensors, radios, displays, and autonomous systems, each with separate interfaces.
Operating this equipment can create significant demands on personnel, particularly when crews must coordinate different systems during fast-moving missions.
Anura is designed to simplify these interactions by allowing operators to communicate goals and instructions in natural language.
The system translates those instructions into individual tasks and coordinates their execution across connected equipment.
It also monitors the results and adjusts activities as operational conditions change.
The platform is intended to support human-machine teaming by reducing the number of separate interfaces operators must manage.
Primordial Labs has integrated Anura with more than a dozen crewed and uncrewed platforms across land and air applications.
In October 2026, the company announced a master teaming agreement with General Dynamics Land Systems.
The partnership is intended to bring Anura to ground combat vehicles across the General Dynamics Land Systems portfolio, including the Abrams tank.
The company is also delivering licenses for small uncrewed aircraft systems to U.S. Army and special operations units.
These licenses are available through the Army’s UAS Marketplace.
Two Small Business Innovation Research Phase III awards received in 2026 expand the company’s work into Army rotary-wing aircraft and the U.S. Air Force’s MQ-9 ground control station.
These projects provide opportunities to demonstrate the platform in different operating environments.
Anura’s architecture is designed to integrate with existing equipment rather than requiring military customers to redesign entire systems.
The approach aligns with the Modular Open Systems Approach, which emphasizes interoperability and flexibility across defense platforms.
Primordial believes this design can help military organizations adopt the technology across different equipment manufacturers and operational environments.
The company’s founders bring experience developing autonomous and AI-enabled technologies at Lockheed Martin.
Co-Founder and CEO Lee Ritholtz and Co-Founder and CTO Adrian Pope previously worked at Lockheed Martin’s Skunk Works.
They participated in the development and deployment of small uncrewed aircraft systems and helped establish the Lockheed Martin Artificial Intelligence Center.
